# Motion timeline, keyframes and easing

- Kind: `editor`
- Category: `vector`
- Slug: `vector/timeline`

## Summary

How animation works in Motion: each animated property of a layer is a track of keyframes with an easing per segment.

## Details

### Animatable properties
- `transform.x`
- `transform.y`
- `transform.scaleX`
- `transform.scaleY`
- `transform.rotation`
- `transform.skewX`
- `transform.skewY`
- `transform.anchorX`
- `transform.anchorY`
- `opacity`
- `fill`
- `stroke`
- `strokeWidth`
- `strokeDashoffset`
- `d`
- `gradientStop[i].color`
- `gradientStop[i].offset`
- `mask`
- `clipPath`
- `filter.blur`
- `motionPath`
transform.x/y move the layer, scaleX/scaleY 1 is the original size, rotation and skew are degrees, opacity 0–1, strokeDashoffset drives draw-on, d is the path shape (morph), motionPath is progress 0–1 along a guide.
### Easing
Presets: linear (Linear), easeIn (Ease in), easeOut (Ease out), easeBoth (Ease in-out), hold (Hold), or a custom cubic-bezier curve. The easing of a segment belongs to the keyframe that starts it; hold keeps the value until the next keyframe.
Good defaults: UI entrances 0.3–0.6 s with ease-out; exits ease-in; loops ease-in-out. Stagger a list by 0.08–0.15 s per item.
The project has a duration, a frame rate and an optional loop; the canvas has a viewBox size (default 512×512 at 24 fps).
